note: Second validation set (R13): fable- and dialogue-shaped stories, written by the builder 2026-10-10 to develop the reader matcher on the shapes B6 uses; never trained on, never a test.

stories.text: A wolf saw a lamb drinking at a stream. The wolf said the lamb was muddying his water. The lamb replied that it stood downstream. The wolf ate the lamb anyway.
qs: Who was drinking at the stream?
What did the wolf say the lamb was doing?

stories.text: An ant worked all summer storing grain. A grasshopper sang in the sun and laughed at her. When winter came, the grasshopper begged the ant for food. The ant gave him a single seed and shut her door.
qs: What did the ant give the grasshopper?

stories.text: "Give me the lantern," said Marta. Her brother Piet handed it over without a word. They walked to the cellar together. Marta found the missing cat behind a barrel and carried it upstairs.
The mouse gnawed through the net and freed the lion. The lion had laughed at the mouse a week before. Now the lion bowed his head and thanked the mouse. The hunters found an empty net at dawn.
qs: What did the mouse gnaw through?
Who had laughed at the mouse?

stories.text: "Is the bridge safe?" asked the traveller. The miller shook his head. "The flood took the middle plank," he said. The traveller crossed by the ford instead and reached the inn by nightfall.
qs: Where did the traveller reach by nightfall?

stories.text: A crow stole a ring from the goldsmith's bench. The goldsmith's daughter, Ines, followed the crow to the church tower. She climbed the tower and found a nest full of rings. Ines returned every ring to the village.
qs: Where did the crow take the ring?
What did Ines find in the tower?
What did Ines return to the village?
